clue.text: Adult, one man's transformed state

indicators.note: transformed says the letters of the preceding words are changed into a new arrangement

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A grown man has undergone a personal transformation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges ADULT, I (one) and MAN; the 's is a link meaning 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamil Nadu is a state in southern India, home of the Tamil language.

clue.text: No one successfully throws this in drier

definitions.text: No one successfully throws this in drier

parts.words: No one successfully throws this in drier
parts.note: to throw in this item is to give up, so nobody who does so succeeds; it is also something used for drying

explanation.surface: Nobody manages to toss this into a tumble dryer.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'throw in the towel' means to concede defeat, so no one who throws it in is successful; 'drier' is a straight hint, a cloth you dry with.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth for drying oneself is exactly what boxers' corners throw into the ring to surrender.

clue.text: Girl married at island golf club

parts.note: the R and A, the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews, written out as R-AND-A

explanation.surface: A girl gets married at a golf club on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The R&A is the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews, Scotland, golf's historic governing body; spelling the ampersand as AND gives RANDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Miranda is a girl's name, famously Prospero's daughter in The Tempest.

clue.text: Strike and pound on wood

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece sitting on another means it comes first

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pound (from Latin libra)
ash is a tree and its timber

explanation.surface: Hit something and hammer on a wooden surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash is to whip or hit hard, a synonym of striking.

clue.text: Soon chapter abandons one of its members

indicators.note: abandons says the chapter's letter leaves the word for a member

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman belonging to a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: A chapter of clergy soon loses one of its members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' refers back to the chapter: a cathedral chapter is the body of canons, so one of its members is a CANON, which then loses C.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is an old-fashioned word meaning shortly or in a little while.

clue.text: Died: duty nurse being replaced by junior

indicators.note: being replaced says the letters are moved into new positions

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A death notice: the duty nurse has been swapped for a more junior colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being replaced' rearranges D (died) with DUTY NURSE; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An understudy is a junior performer who learns a lead's part, ready to stand in.

clue.text: Mousy girl college rejected

indicators.note: rejected says the pieces are turned back to front

parts.note: Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: A shy girl turned down by a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousy describes a quiet, shy, nervous person, a synonym of timid.

clue.text: Where Anne Boleyn died, now modern flats

definitions.meaning: Henry VIII's second wife was executed within the Tower of London, the block being the place of beheading

explanation.surface: A historic execution site has been redeveloped into modern apartments.
explanation.walkthrough: Anne Boleyn was beheaded at the Tower of London in 1536; the Tower plus the executioner's block gives the first reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall residential building of many apartments is a high-rise, common in British post-war housing.

clue.text: Husband hopefully has power, owning two castles

indicators.note: owning says the power word holds the castles inside it

parts.note: might means power or strength
R is the chess notation for rook, the piece also called castle, so two give RR

explanation.surface: A prospective husband who is powerful and owns two castles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link; the two castles are chess rooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Right is the ideal man someone hopes to marry, so a hoped-for spouse.

clue.text: Made out record brought in money, without advance

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: without says a letter is dropped from the money word

parts.note: earned means received money for work
A is short for advance, as in the A of an advance payment abbreviation

explanation.surface: A record earned money, though no advance was paid.
explanation.definitionFit: To make out something faint is to perceive or spot it, which is to discern it.

clue.text: What Hamlet was reading: several worthless poets?

definitions.meaning: Hamlet's reply when Polonius asks what he reads, in Act 2
a few copies of the poet Wordsworth, each with its worth taken away

explanation.surface: A literary question: what was Hamlet reading — some poor-quality poets?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: William Wordsworth, the English Romantic poet, without WORTH leaves WORDS, and several of him give it three times.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's famous evasive reply to Polonius names his reading matter as mere verbiage.

clue.text: Hutton's eyepiece?

definitions.meaning: belonging to Len Hutton, the England cricket captain of the 1950s
the glass part of a spyglass or microscope

explanation.surface: An optical part belonging to someone called Hutton.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Len Hutton was a famous Yorkshire and England batsman, so something of his is Len's.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of curved glass through which the eye looks is one part of an eyepiece.

clue.text: Urge poor to revolt and interrupt parliament

indicators.note: to revolt suggests overturning, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A call to the poor to rise up and halt parliament's work.
explanation.definitionFit: To prorogue is to suspend a parliamentary session without dissolving the legislature.

clue.text: Sudden withdrawal of post-Christmas sandwich?

definitions.meaning: leftover roast bird eaten chilled after the festive dinner

explanation.surface: A sandwich made from festive leftovers, with talk of withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading: leftover chilled poultry from the Christmas roast.
explanation.definitionFit: Quitting an addiction abruptly rather than tapering off is the idiomatic sense of this phrase.

clue.text: Joke brings judge appalling disrepute

indicators.note: appalling suggests something badly mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A joke lands a judge in dreadful disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brings' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeu d'esprit is a light-hearted witty remark or piece of writing, French for a game of the mind.

clue.text: An actor warning cast finally, when he twigs

parts.note: an gives the indefinite article A
a ham is an overacting performer
an omen is a sign warning of what is to come

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word cast

explanation.surface: A performer warns the cast at the very end, at the moment he realises.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'twig' is British slang for to understand suddenly.
explanation.definitionFit: An aha moment is the instant of sudden realisation, the point where understanding dawns.

clue.text: Blamed IRA for explosion? Excellent

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A news report blaming the IRA for a bombing, with an odd word of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: The IRA was the Irish Republican Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Admirable means deserving praise, close to outstanding or excellent.

clue.text: Endlessly rubbishing what Horace wrote

indicators.note: endlessly says the critic's word loses both its end letters

parts.note: slating is harshly criticising, rubbishing

explanation.surface: Someone is endlessly running down the work of the Roman poet Horace.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace was a Roman poet of the Augustan age, so his works are in the classical language of Rome.

clue.text: Contemplated minute and second hand

parts.note: used goods are second-hand, previously owned

explanation.surface: Someone pondered a clock's minute and second hands.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests clock hands, but 'second hand' means pre-owned.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to think deeply or ponder, so mused is a synonym of pondered.

clue.text: Fish very important in church

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: in says the important word goes inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
key means crucial or important

explanation.surface: A fish turns up as a VIP in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very important' reads as one phrase, as in VIP, but the two words are clued separately; CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: The sockeye is a species of Pacific salmon with red flesh.

clue.text: Hard-working lower classes ordered to waste time

parts.note: D and E are the lowest grades in British social classification

indicators.note: to waste suggests throwing away, so the time letter is removed

parts.note: dictated means commanded or ordered

explanation.surface: The working classes were told to idle away the hours.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's market-research social grades run A, B, C1, C2, D, E, so D and E are the lower classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dedicated person is committed and conscientious, devoted to the job.

clue.text: Business is booming, so get something more expensive

definitions.meaning: commerce rising, read as trade going up
exchange an item for a costlier one

explanation.surface: Commerce is thriving, so one buys something pricier.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange a possession for a higher-value one, or commerce increasing, are both senses of this phrase.

clue.text: Swear a second time to tour old resort

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the oath word goes around the old letter

parts.note: re-curse, to swear again

explanation.surface: A tourist swears again on going round an old holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday destination but means an expedient you turn to.
explanation.definitionFit: Recourse is a source of help to turn to, as in 'a last resort'.

clue.text: Like a tie, or like some underwear?

definitions.meaning: resembling a shoelace or other cord used for tying
made of delicate openwork fabric, as lingerie often is

explanation.surface: Asking whether something resembles a necktie or underclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: A lace is a cord for tying shoes, so 'like a tie' means lace-like in that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something resembling or made of lace, both the cord and the delicate fabric.

clue.text: Siberian beast of burden extremely unfit

parts.note: a yak is a Himalayan ox used to carry loads

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme letters, the first and last, of the word unfit

explanation.surface: A Siberian pack animal is in very poor shape.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yakuts are a Turkic people of the Sakha Republic in northeastern Siberia.

clue.text: Make leather with good smell

parts.note: to tan is to treat hide into leather

explanation.surface: Tanning hides gives off a pleasant odour.
explanation.definitionFit: A tang is a sharp, distinctive taste or odour.

clue.text: Help with second letter, having misplaced the first

indicators.note: misplaced says the letter has been put in a different position

parts.note: beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet
A is alpha, the first letter, which ends the word beta

explanation.surface: Helping with the second letter after losing the first one.
explanation.walkthrough: The A of BETA is moved from the end to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage, typically in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Turn at snooker with rest, to interrupt Tennyson's work

parts.note: a break is a player's continuous scoring visit to the table
a break is a pause or rest
to break is to interrupt

explanation.surface: A snooker turn and a pause interrupt a reading of Tennyson.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker is a cue sport; 'rest' also misleads, since a rest is a cue support in snooker. Tennyson's poem begins 'Break, break, break, / On thy cold gray stones, O Sea!'
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Tennyson wrote the elegy of that title in 1842, mourning his friend Arthur Hallam.

clue.text: Abrasive gallery remembers revolutionary exhibits

indicators.note: revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
exhibits says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A harsh gallery recalls its revolutionary exhibitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Emery is a granular rock used as an abrasive, as on emery boards for nails.

clue.text: Tricky situation getting leggings to meet belly

parts.note: tights are close-fitting legwear
a pot is a protruding stomach, a pot belly

explanation.surface: Pulling on leggings over a big stomach is awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' and 'to meet' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A tight spot is an idiom for a difficult predicament.
